items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and the public API is well documented. The cap applies, though: business logic uses single-letter names such as `s := &b.durable`, `j := &t.mu.jobs[...]`, `var m base.SeqNum` and `w`. Formatting matches pebble style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go (427 lines) holds a self-contained durabilityTracker built from short functions: wait, notify, record, close, stats. Constants are named and the waiters use a heap. The notify call is split between applyInternal and SyncWait, and reflect-based handler detection is a little hacky, but both are minor.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Context cancellation is handled correctly: a durability or close result wins over cancellation (`if w.index >= 0 ... return <-w.ch`). Subscriptions and job retention have named bounds. Errors are wrapped with errors.Wrapf. A failure latches firstErr and fails all waiters. Close resolves every waiter. Concurrency is protected by a mutex.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: All changes are additive: new fields, methods and EnsureDefaults noop. Non-sync commits pay only one extra crtime.NowMono for applyDuration. Sync commits take the tracker mutex once, which the wait APIs need. NoSyncWait still never blocks, and its notification is deferred to SyncWait. Existing callbacks are unchanged.
